openQuestions.q: Should the NEW quorum_submit drift-accept guard predicate (CHK-002) independently apply the EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH no-signal exclusion, given the floor function it is asked to mirror (eventsWithStoryFilesHashDowngrade, review-escalation.ts:948-969) does NOT itself implement that guard (unlike its three siblings), and fixing the floor is explicitly excluded scope for this story?
openQuestions.evidence: decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md "Adopted Bindings" lists "review escalation host verdicts and degraded fallback records" as one of three adopted storyFilesHash bindings. decisions/review-run-binding-race.md: "the storyFilesHash drift-advisory downgrade must treat EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH (sha256 of an empty story-owned diff) as no-signal on BOTH the stored and the live side and fall through to strict materialHash, exactly as delivery-check-hash.ts:184-188 already does" (scoped to "checkEvidenceFreshnessForGit, all callers"). Source: packages/main/src/core/evidence-freshness.ts:9-19 defines EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH and states "Callers that key the advisory on storyFilesHash must therefore treat this empty-set value as no-signal". packages/main/src/core/review-escalation.ts eventsWithStoryFilesHashDowngrade (lines 948-969) only guards `!currentStoryFilesHash` and `!storyFilesHash` (falsy/missing), never `=== EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH` (a real, truthy sha256('') digest) -- it is NOT a caller of checkEvidenceFreshnessForGit and was not touched by the review-run-binding-race fix. CHK-002 verification-intent (happy/edge/adversarial) never mentions EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH, and plan.md's predicate text ("same materialDigest OR (stale materialDigest but storyFilesHash equal to the current storyFilesHash)") has no such exclusion either.
openQuestions.resolution: The new quorum_submit guard faithfully mirrors the floor predicate AS IT IS, including its lack of an EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH no-signal exclusion. Rationale: the guard exists to refuse exactly the set of resubmissions the floor would drift-accept (docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md lists review escalation host verdicts as an adopted storyFilesHash binding); if the guard unilaterally added the EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH exclusion that eventsWithStoryFilesHashDowngrade (core/review-escalation.ts:948-969) does not have, an empty-story-diff corner would let a resubmit through while the floor still drift-accepts the old verdicts, recreating the B-bf52 poisoning in that corner. The guard additionally skips legacy events whose storyFilesHash field is absent/blank (no signal, no collision claim). Adding the EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH no-signal guard to the FLOOR (per review-run-binding-race.md mandatory-guard guidance) is a floor-semantics change, which is explicitly excluded scope for B-3144; when a future story adds it to the floor, the quorum guard must be updated in lockstep, and the guard comment will say so.
